title: A supplier catalogue of 200,000 rows in the browser
summary: Let a buyer scroll, sort, filter and bulk-edit a huge table without the browser giving up.
context: Cubbon Traders' buyers work in a catalogue of 200,000 items: prices, suppliers, pack sizes. They scroll, filter by several columns and change prices in bulk. The page now loads 5,000 rows and has a search box for the rest.
They would rather export to a spreadsheet than use it, and then the data comes back with errors. Some use old office laptops, and others are editing the same rows at the same time.
must_handle: Scrolling stays smooth on a modest laptop.
A filter on several columns answers within a second or so.
A bulk change to 3,000 rows shows progress, and can partly fail.
A person's place, filter and sort survive a reload and can be shared as a link.
A row someone else changed is not silently overwritten.
show_in_answer: The API the table needs: its paging, filters and bulk edit.
How rows are held in the browser and what is drawn.
What is cached, and how it is invalidated after an edit.
How a bulk edit reports partial failure.
